name: Lemon Méringue Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: large lemon—juice and half the rind, grated
ingredients.originalText: 1 large lemon—juice and half the rind, grated

instructions.text: Soak the bread in the milk; add the beaten yolks, with the butter and sugar rubbed to a cream, also the lemon.
Bake in a buttered dish until firm and slightly brown.
Draw to the door of the oven and cover with a méringue of the whites whipped to a froth with three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar, and a little lemon-juice.
Brown very slightly; sift powdered sugar over it, and eat cold.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak the bread in the milk; add the beaten yolks, with the butter and sugar rubbed to a cream, also the lemon.
2. Bake in a buttered dish until firm and slightly brown.
3. Draw to the door of the oven and cover with a méringue of the whites whipped to a froth with three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar, and a little lemon-juice.
4. Brown very slightly; sift powdered sugar over it, and eat cold.
